verses.text: Samuel's word reached all Israel. Israel went out to fight the Philistines and camped near Ebenezer, while the Philistines camped at Aphek.
The Philistines lined up against Israel. When the fighting began, they defeated Israel and killed about four thousand men on the battlefield.

When the troops returned to camp, Israel's elders asked, “Why did the LORD let the Philistines defeat us today? Let's bring the ark of the LORD's covenant from Shiloh. If it's here among us, it can save us from our enemies.”
So they sent to Shiloh and brought back the ark of the covenant of the LORD of Armies, who sits enthroned above the cherubim. Eli's sons Hophni and Phinehas were there with God's ark of the covenant.
When the ark of the LORD's covenant entered the camp, all Israel shouted so loudly the ground shook.
The Philistines heard the roar and asked, “What does all that shouting in the Hebrews' camp mean?” Then they found out the LORD's ark had come into the camp.
They were afraid and said, “God has come into their camp. We're in trouble! Nothing like this has ever happened before.
We're doomed! Who can save us from these mighty gods? These are the gods that struck the Egyptians with every kind of plague in the wilderness.
Be strong, Philistines! Fight like men, or you'll become slaves to the Hebrews just as they've been slaves to you. Stand your ground and fight!”
The Philistines fought and defeated Israel, and each man fled to his own tent. It was a terrible slaughter. Thirty thousand Israelite foot soldiers fell.
God's ark was captured, and Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, were killed.
That same day a man from Benjamin ran from the battle to Shiloh with his clothes torn and dirt on his head.
When he arrived, Eli was sitting by the road watching, worried sick about God's ark. When the man reached town and told what had happened, the whole town cried out.
Eli heard the uproar and asked, “What is all that noise?” The man hurried over to tell him.
Eli was ninety-eight years old. His eyes stared straight ahead, and he couldn't see.
The man said, “I've come from the army. I ran from the battlefield today.” Eli asked, “What happened, my son?”
The messenger answered, “Israel ran from the Philistines, and many of our people were killed. Your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead too, and God's ark has been captured.”
At the mention of God's ark, Eli fell backward off his seat beside the gate. He was old and heavy, and the fall broke his neck and killed him. He had judged Israel forty years.

His daughter-in-law, Phinehas's wife, was pregnant and close to giving birth. When she heard that God's ark had been captured and that her husband and father-in-law were dead, she doubled over as labor came on and gave birth.
As she was dying, the women standing beside her said, “Don't be afraid. You've had a son.” She didn't answer or pay attention.
She named the boy Ichabod, saying, “The glory has left Israel!” She said this because God's ark was captured and her husband and father-in-law were dead.
She said, “The glory has left Israel because God's ark has been captured.”
